description: Oman Ministry of Health mandatory health insurance coverage requirements under Royal Decree 11/2021 (Health Insurance Law) and MOH implementing regulations. All health insurance policies issued in the Sultanate of Oman must comply with these minimum benefit standards. Non-compliant exclusions, copayment structures, or benefit limits are void and unenforceable under Omani law.

clauses.title: Mandatory Inpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies in the Sultanate of Oman must provide inpatient coverage including medical and surgical treatment, room and board at a minimum general ward level, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, diagnostic investigations performed during hospitalization, prescribed medications administered during the inpatient stay, blood transfusions, and physiotherapy directly related to the admission. Coverage must extend to all MOH-licensed network hospitals within Oman. The maximum copayment for any inpatient admission shall not exceed OMR 10 per admission, and the total annual inpatient copayment burden shall not exceed OMR 300 per member per policy year. Exclusion of inpatient care for acute medical conditions is strictly prohibited.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 7 — Minimum inpatient benefit standards; MOH Circular 04/2019

clauses.title: Mandatory Outpatient Coverage
clauses.full_text: Outpatient consultations with general practitioners and specialists must be covered under all health insurance policies in Oman. Diagnostic services including laboratory tests and basic radiology must be included. The maximum copayment for outpatient services shall not exceed 20% of the eligible claim amount and shall not exceed OMR 3 per visit. Insurers may not impose copayment amounts above OMR 3 per outpatient visit for services within the mandatory benefits package. Coverage must include follow-up consultations, chronic disease management, and preventive health screenings as prescribed by MOH guidelines.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 8; MOH Implementing Regulation 12/2019 — Outpatient benefit minimums

clauses.title: Mandatory Emergency Treatment
clauses.full_text: Emergency treatment must be covered at all MOH-licensed facilities within the Sultanate of Oman without requirement of prior authorization. Insurers may not deny emergency claims on the grounds of lack of pre-authorization or treatment at a non-network facility within Oman. No copayment shall apply to genuine emergency admissions. Post-emergency notification by the insured or the treating facility within 24 hours of admission is acceptable in lieu of prior authorization. Emergency treatment at non-network facilities within Oman must be reimbursed at not less than network-equivalent rates. Refusal to cover stabilization and life-saving treatment constitutes a violation of MOH regulations.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 12 — Emergency services; MOH Circular 08/2019 — Pre-authorization exemptions

clauses.title: Mandatory Maternity Benefits
clauses.full_text: Health insurance policies in the Sultanate of Oman must cover maternity benefits including normal delivery, caesarean section, antenatal consultations (minimum 6 visits), postnatal care, and pregnancy-related complications. The waiting period for maternity benefits must not exceed 12 months from the date of continuous coverage. Newborn care for the first 30 days from birth must be included under the mother's policy without additional premium or separate enrollment. The minimum benefit limit for normal delivery shall be OMR 1,500 and for caesarean section OMR 2,500. Exclusion of pregnancy-related complications, including ectopic pregnancy and gestational diabetes, is prohibited under MOH regulations.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 10; MOH Circular 15/2019 — Maternity benefit standards and waiting period caps

clauses.title: Mandatory Pharmacy Coverage
clauses.full_text: Prescribed medications for covered conditions must be covered under all health insurance policies in Oman. The maximum copayment for brand-name medications shall not exceed 25% of the eligible medication cost. The maximum copayment for generic medications shall not exceed 15% of the eligible medication cost. Medications prescribed and administered during a covered inpatient stay must be covered at 100% with no additional copayment applied to the insured. Coverage must extend to medications listed on the Oman MOH Essential Drug List and the Oman National Formulary. Insurers must encourage generic substitution where clinically appropriate but may not mandate generic use when the prescribing physician certifies medical necessity for a brand-name medication.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 9; MOH Pharmaceutical Regulation 06/2019 — Drug coverage and copayment limits

clauses.title: Maximum Copayment Caps
clauses.full_text: The MOH mandates the following maximum copayment caps which no insurer operating in the Sultanate of Oman may exceed: Outpatient consultation: 20% of the eligible amount, maximum OMR 3 per visit. Emergency services: OMR 0 (no copayment permitted). Inpatient admission: maximum OMR 10 per admission (flat copay). Annual out-of-pocket maximum for mandatory benefits: OMR 1,500 per member per policy year. Any policy applying copayment amounts above these regulatory caps renders the excess amount void and the insurer is liable for reimbursement of the difference to the insured member. Repeated violations are subject to penalties under Article 25 of Royal Decree 11/2021.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 14 — Financial obligations of insured persons; MOH Circular 10/2019

clauses.title: Minimum Annual Benefit Limit
clauses.full_text: All health insurance policies in the Sultanate of Oman must provide a minimum annual benefit limit of OMR 30,000 per member per policy year for mandatory coverage benefits. Policies may not impose annual sub-limits on individual mandatory benefits below the following minimums: Emergency treatment: OMR 30,000 per incident. Maternity — normal delivery: OMR 1,500 per pregnancy. Maternity — caesarean section: OMR 2,500 per pregnancy. Policies with annual benefit limits below OMR 30,000 are deemed non-compliant and subject to suspension by the MOH. Insurers must clearly disclose all benefit limits in the policy schedule provided to the insured member at the time of enrollment.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 8 — Minimum coverage thresholds; MOH Regulation 14/2019

clauses.title: Prohibited Exclusions — Conditions Insurers May Not Exclude
clauses.full_text: The following conditions and treatments may not be excluded from coverage under any MOH-compliant health insurance policy in the Sultanate of Oman: (a) HIV/AIDS treatment and management for legally resident insured members, including antiretroviral therapy and associated laboratory monitoring; (b) Mental health acute inpatient treatment — a minimum of 10 days per policy year must be covered for psychiatric conditions requiring hospitalization; (c) Dialysis for chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease, including hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis; (d) Cancer screening tests as recommended by the Oman National Cancer Screening Programme, including mammography, cervical screening, and colorectal screening. Any policy clause purporting to exclude these conditions or treatments is void and unenforceable under Omani law. Insurers found in violation are subject to penalties under Article 25 of Royal Decree 11/2021.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 11; MOH Ministerial Decision 22/2019 — Prohibited exclusions under mandatory coverage

clauses.title: Maximum Waiting Period Caps
clauses.full_text: Waiting periods for pre-existing diseases and conditions under MOH-compliant health insurance policies in Oman may not exceed 6 months from the date of continuous coverage commencement. Insurers may not impose any waiting period, including initial waiting periods, for the following: emergency treatment regardless of cause, maternity complications including ectopic pregnancy, pre-eclampsia, and emergency caesarean section. Transfer of coverage between MOH-approved insurers must carry over completed waiting periods — insurers may not restart or extend waiting periods for members transferring from another compliant policy. The burden of proving a pre-existing condition rests with the insurer and must be supported by documented medical evidence obtained prior to the policy inception date.
clauses.regulatory_note: Royal Decree 11/2021, Article 13; MOH Circular 11/2019 — Waiting period restrictions and portability requirements
